ai.description: This frog reaches 4–5 cm. It is bright green with black-spotted yellow flanks and distinct red webbing between its toes. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus pseudomalabaricus* is uniquely distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow reticulated pattern covering its dark brown dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: The Anaimalai flying frog inhabits evergreen rainforests and high-altitude shola forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anaimalai flying frog is primarily nocturnal, using its large, fully webbed feet to glide between trees to forage for insects and escape potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Anaimalai flying frog breeds during the monsoon, laying a clutch of 50–100 eggs inside a foam nest attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anaimalai flying frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the Anaimalai Hills across the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Anaimalai flying frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams during the monsoon.
